title: Burn — 578 Squadron Memorial Panels, Burn Methodist Chapel
memorial_type: Board/plaque/tablet: eleven stainless steel plaques on a backboard in a glazed stainless steel frame
memorial_address: Burn Methodist Chapel, Main Street, Burn, Selby, North Yorkshire, YO8 8LJ
inscription: 219 members of aircrew killed, 79 shot down and taken prisoner of war, 45 aircraft lost on active service; presented by the 578 Burn Association to the people of Burn
crew_summary: 219 aircrew killed, 79 taken prisoner, 45 aircraft lost — 578 Squadron at RAF Burn January 1944 to March 1945
narrative: 578 Squadron formed at RAF Burn in North Yorkshire in January 1944 and flew Halifax bombers until the end of the war. In just fourteen months of operations from Burn, 219 aircrew were killed, 79 became prisoners of war, and 45 aircraft were lost — a savage toll for a single station. The memorial panels in Burn Methodist Chapel were dedicated in May 1999, fifty-four years after the squadron's disbandment. Eleven stainless steel plaques mounted on a glazed backboard record every name of those killed. The memorial is maintained by Burn Village Council and stands as a permanent record of the human cost of Bomber Command operations from this quiet North Yorkshire village. RAF Burn — now farmland — saw many notable operations including crew of the Farnsfield Halifax MZ519 (also 578 Squadron) who flew from this station.
memorial_details: Eleven stainless steel plaques on a backboard, in a glazed stainless steel frame, hang in Burn Methodist Chapel. They record 219 aircrew of 578 Squadron killed, with 79 taken prisoner and 45 aircraft lost. The memorial was designed by the architect Hugh Cawdron, cost 750 pounds, and was unveiled and dedicated on 16 May 1999 by Rev Owain Williams. The 578 Burn Association presented it to the people of Burn. IWM names Burn Village Council as custodian. A separate roadside stone to the squadron stands on the A19 opposite the Wheatsheaf Inn.
